failures.evidence: RED TEST, committed in this round: `packages/daemon/internal/supervise/reopen_resumes_session_test.go`, `TestAReopenedClosedClaimResumesTheSessionItKept`. It closes a claim's issue, restarts the machine, retries the claim, and asserts the launch is a Resume. At this head: `--- FAIL`, reporting `the reopened claim was launched with Spawn, want Resume`. Copied unchanged onto the previous head 03005ece: `--- PASS`. So the merge introduced it. It is the only failure in the whole `internal/supervise` package here (`go test ./internal/supervise/ -count=1` → that one `--- FAIL`). WHY, read in the code rather than inferred: the merge added `clearIssueResumePath` (table.go:1464), which sets `m.claim.SessionFile = ""`, and both `issueClose` (table.go:1422) and `issueCloseRetired` (table.go:1434) call it; at 03005ece `issueClose` cleared nothing and `clearIssueResumePath` did not exist (`git show 03005ece:...table.go | grep -c clearIssueResumePath` → 0). `Machine.start` (machine.go:1238) then branches `if m.claim.SessionFile == "" { return m.deps.Runtime.Spawn(...) }`, so the reopen spawns. The retained session id reaches NO runtime as a resume handle, which I checked four ways: `runtime.SpawnSpec` carries only `ResumeSessionFile` and no id field; daemon's real `specs.SpawnSpec` (specs.go:88) reads `c.Session` only at specs.go:217, a Kubernetes plugin-install condition; the Sandbox manifest reads Claude Code's resume id `by the id prepare read from the recorded path` (manifest.go:443), so a cleared path gives `--session-id <fresh uuid>`; and `reap_guard.go:26-30` reads the id as the volume's evidence, which is exactly what `issueClose`'s own comment says it is kept for. BOTH RUNTIMES, as the architect's addition requires: Oh My Pi resumes by `ResumeSessionFile`, and the tmux runtime searches its folders for that same path (spawn.go's resume), so with the path gone neither has anything to find and each spawns. The shipped test `TestAClaimAnIssueCloseRetiredRelaunchesOnItsSessionWithNoVolume` (issue_close_test.go:115) is NEW in this merge (absent at 03005ece) and asserts `h.wantCalls("Resume", 0)` with a `Spawn`, so it pins the fresh agent rather than catching it; its comment says 'The session the claim kept reaches the new process through the spec instead', and the assertion behind that clause is `built.Session == session`, which only checks the Claim handed to the spec builder still carries the id — not that any launch resumes it, which the real builder does not. FIX, for the implementer to choose: either carry the session id to the runtimes as a resume handle (a field on `runtime.SpawnSpec`, honoured by both, with the tmux runtime finding the file by id as the architect's addition describes) and keep the path cleared; or stop clearing the path on close. The first is what the merge's own comments promise.
